findings.where: Article specimen, the title 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law' (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The apostrophe in 'World's' looks like a straight typewriter tick. The rest of the article uses curly quotes (‘chapter topics’, “What is the best…”), so at title size the one straight mark is the largest piece of punctuation on the page and the only one set wrong.
findings.who_objects: The founder, and the reader the direction is aimed at. This tile sells 'the editorial gravitas of a legal journal', and a journal never sets a typewriter apostrophe in a headline. A careful reader at a development bank sees it at once, and it makes the type look unfinished.

findings.where: First screen header, desktop: the nav (Profile, Articles, Blog) beside the name 'Mark M. Moseley' and the credential line
findings.fault: The nav sits between the name's baseline and the credential line's, so it lines up with neither. It looks centred on the two-line block rather than set on a baseline, and the top band reads slightly adrift.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who judges the first screen first. A direction built on a document's quiet precision needs its header lines to share a baseline. A floating nav makes the top of the sheet look less carefully set than the heading below it.

findings.where: First screen on phone: the portrait inside the hairline frame
findings.fault: On desktop the portrait sits flush against the frame, and the tile's own texture note says it should ('the portrait set flush against it'). On phone it floats inset inside the frame. Its left edge is a few pixels in from the logo, heading and paragraph, so it lines up with neither the frame nor the text column.
findings.who_objects: The founder comparing the two widths. The frame and photograph are the direction's one borrowed detail, and here they are treated two ways. The near-miss with the text edge also looks like a mistake, not a choice.

findings.where: Placeholder captions: the hero portrait on desktop (right-aligned, outside the frame), the hero portrait on phone (centred), the article photograph (left-aligned)
findings.fault: The same small caption is set three ways: right-aligned, centred and left-aligned. Elsewhere the sheet aligns everything left.
findings.who_objects: The founder, and Angélique, who will add captions to future articles. Like parts should look alike, and the centred phone caption is the only centred text on the sheet, so it reads as a different kind of note.

findings.where: Palette, the 'Pad yellow' swatch (desktop and phone)
findings.fault: The yellow swatch has a darker olive edge, a colour that is not in the palette. The blue and grey swatches have no edge, and the paper swatch's edge is the grey hairline. The address strip it stands for has no such edge on the first screen.
findings.who_objects: The founder reading the palette as the tile's colour claim. The sheet says grey, blue, paper and yellow are the only colours, and the swatch adds a fifth tone. That olive appears nowhere in use.
